quotes.text: Excel was never meant to be the world's data hub. It was built for grids, not governance, a sandbox for accountants that somehow became the backbone of global analytics.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains in one image why spreadsheets become a data quality problem.

quotes.text: Excel's architecture encourages this disaster. It has no schema enforcement, no input validation, no relational discipline.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the structural reasons behind messy spreadsheet data.

quotes.text: Most users linger in chat wondering why nothing changes, and they are basically talking to their analyst and ignoring the janitor holding the tools.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Points out the common mistake of using only the chat mode instead of letting Copilot edit the sheet.

quotes.text: Treat copilot as a preprocessor, not a crutch. People misuse it like spellcheck, fixing errors after they happen.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a clear recommendation to use Copilot at the start of the data lifecycle.

quotes.text: Once AI assumes drudgery, your value migrates to interpretation, and you're not the data janitor anymore. You're the data conductor.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Describes how the analyst role shifts once cleanup is automated.

takeaways: Excel's flexibility without schema or validation is the root of inconsistent data that breaks Power BI, Power Automate and Fabric downstream.
Copilot in Excel only edits the sheet when you move beyond chat and give it clear commands to normalize, validate and transform data.
Embedding Copilot prompts at the start of every dataset's lifecycle turns cleanup into an automatic preflight check and frees analysts for real analysis.
hook: Analysts lose hours every week fixing dates, trailing spaces and mismatched labels before any real analysis can start. This episode is for Excel users and data teams who feed Power BI and Power Automate. It shows how Copilot in Excel can normalize, validate and transform data with a few prompts so cleanup stops being manual work.
